title: Stalemate in mixed endings: save the draw, avoid the trap
outcomes: Finds the stalemate resource for the losing side when the theme is not named
Avoids the quiet move that stalemates when ahead
Counts the opponent's legal moves after a candidate move before playing it
Recognises an ending where stalemate cannot arise

steps.text:
In *Stalemate as a rescue* you were told to look for the stalemate. Now the theme is not named and either side may need the idea.
**Behind:** can I give up a piece so that, after it is taken, I have no legal move and am not in check?
**Ahead:** does my quiet move leave the opponent with no legal move?
Both are one count of the legal moves of the side that would be left to move.

steps.caption: White to move. Two quiet queen moves would stalemate Black.

line.say: Checkmate: the king on g6 covers g7 and h7, and the queen covers the back rank.

claims.statement: Qh6 would be a stalemate: the tablebase gives a draw.
Qf6 would be a stalemate: the tablebase gives a draw.

steps.text:
**When it works:** the opponent has to take the piece (a check forces it) or has nothing better, and afterwards the side to move has no legal move with any piece and is not in check. **Rule of thumb:** it happens mostly with a king on the edge or in a corner.
**Test before every quiet move:** one black pawn or piece that can still move ends the stalemate, for the trick and for the trap.

steps.title: The same queen move, one spare move
